report.summary: Checkout-service and api-gateway error rates stepped up abruptly at 16:00 UTC on 2026-09-04 (checkout about 21%, gateway about 8%), with customers reporting failed payments. The system determination is CONCLUSIVE at confidence 0.70 with a margin of 0.60 over the runner-up hypothesis, and 12 verified supporting items against 1 contradicting item. The leading hypothesis is that payment-service's outbound calls to the external provider api.payprovider.example/v2/charges began failing with 503s at about 16:00:02Z, and checkout and the gateway pass these failures through as 502s. Payment-service's own CPU, memory, request rate and payments-db metrics were flat, and the provider reported degraded status at 16:28. The exact layer that converts provider 503s into the 502s seen by checkout is not identified, and the count mismatch (60 checkout 502s versus 35 payment-service 503 errors) remains unexplained. The provider's incident details were not retrieved, so the provider-side cause is unconfirmed.

root_cause.mechanism: Payment-service's outbound calls to the external provider api.payprovider.example/v2/charges begin failing with 503 at about 16:00:02Z after three attempts, driving its error rate from 0.17% to about 39% and p99 latency from 464 ms to about 9.9 s. Checkout's payment calls then fail and checkout returns 502 to api-gateway, which passes these through as its own 5xx.
assumptions: The provider 503s are the cause of payment-service failures rather than a client-side retry or configuration fault
The 'payment-service returned 502' text in checkout logs is a translation of upstream payment failures by a layer between checkout and payment-service

Checkout's payment calls then fail and checkout returns 502 to api-gateway, which passes these through as its own 5xx.
assumptions: The provider 503s are the cause of payment-service failures rather than a client-side retry or configuration fault
The 'payment-service returned 502' text in checkout logs is a translation of upstream payment failures by a layer between checkout and payment-service

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: An expired or unrenewed certificate on the checkout-to-payment-service TLS path would cause handshake failures surfacing as 502s while plain HTTP /health stays 200. This would match P06 but would not explain payment-service's own ERROR logs citing provider 503s.
assumptions: Certificate expiry coincides with 16:00Z
The provider 503s are a separate parallel problem

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: A payments-db connection or query problem would slow payment-service and cause payment timeouts, as in P07.
assumptions: Payment-service-side connection pool metrics would show saturation if they were queried

observed_facts.statement: checkout-service error_rate rose from about 0.35% at 15:55 to 21.17% in the 16:00 bucket and stayed between about 19.9% and 22.5% through 16:30.
api-gateway error_rate rose from about 0.35% at 15:55 to 7.73% at 16:00 and stayed between about 7.5% and 8.3% through 16:30; gateway CPU, memory, latency and request rate showed no step change.
payment-service error_rate rose from 0.17% at 15:55 to 39.13% at 16:00 and stayed near 40% through 16:30; latency_p99 rose from about 464 ms to about 9857 ms in the same bucket.

The first payment-service ERROR is at 16:00:02Z: a 503 Service Unavailable from api.payprovider.example/v2/charges on attempt 3/3; all returned payment-service ERRORs carry this signature and none report a 502.

The first api-gateway ERROR is at 16:00:12Z (upstream checkout-service returned 502 on POST /api/v1/checkout), and the first checkout-service ERROR is at 16:00:27Z (payment-service returned 502 Bad Gateway).
payment-service CPU, memory and request rate stayed in normal ranges across 15:50 to 16:30; payments-db connections, CPU, query latency, disk and replication lag showed no change at or after 16:00.
payment-service logged circuit breaker 'payment-provider' CLOSED to OPEN transitions at 16:02:04Z, 16:10:06Z, 16:17:50Z and 16:25:02Z.

The external payment provider's status page reported 'Elevated error rates on Charges API' (investigating) at 16:28Z; no change record exists for payment-service, checkout-service or api-gateway near onset, and the only change in the window is an unrelated search-service deploy at 15:40Z.
Health checks at 16:28Z returned HTTP 200 for checkout-service, payment-service and api-gateway, but these are shallow /health checks.

assumptions: The provider 503 responses are the cause of payment-service failures rather than a client-side retry or configuration fault.
A layer between checkout and payment-service (proxy, HTTP client or retry logic) converts upstream failures into the 502 text seen in checkout logs; no logs from that layer were checked.
The api-gateway error_rate metric approximates its 5xx rate, though its exact definition is not confirmed.
Five-minute metric resolution and sampled logs are sufficient to order the first errors, though sub-bucket ordering is uncertain.
Shallow /health checks do not exercise payment writes or TLS, so they do not confirm payment path health.

inferred_conclusions.statement: The incident is most probably driven by an upstream failure at the external payment provider (api.payprovider.example) returning 503s, which payment-service surfaces and checkout and the gateway propagate as 5xx errors.
payments-db and payment-service resource exhaustion are unlikely causes, since their metrics and logs show no change or timeouts toward payment-service.
The api-gateway 5xx is a pass-through of checkout-service 502s rather than an independent gateway fault, since gateway resource metrics are normal.

The 502 translation layer is not identified and the 60 checkout 502s versus 35 payment-service 503s count mismatch is unexplained, so some checkout failures may have causes not visible in payment-service logs.

Certificate expiry on the checkout-to-payment-service TLS path is a low-probability alternative, since no certificate change is recorded, but expiry dates and handshake telemetry were not available to rule it out.
No recent deploy or config change on checkout-service, api-gateway or payment-service lands near onset, so the trigger is most likely external.

remediation.action: Enable or confirm the provider failover or fallback path for payment charges, and communicate status to affected customers while the provider degrades.
remediation.rationale: Provider 503s on attempt 3/3 are the observed failing hop and the provider reports elevated Charges API errors.

remediation.action: Hold or queue retries of failed checkouts so customers are not charged twice when the provider recovers.
remediation.rationale: Failed payments are reported by customers and retries against a degraded provider can create duplicate charges.

remediation.rationale: Provider-side cause and recovery timing are unverified and would confirm or revise the leading hypothesis.

remediation.action: Identify the component that maps provider 503 to checkout's 502 and add logging of upstream status codes at that hop.
remediation.rationale: The translation layer and the 60 versus 35 count mismatch are the main open gaps in the causal chain.

remediation.action: Review payment-service retry, timeout and circuit-breaker settings against provider behaviour, and tune them to fail fast under provider outages.
remediation.rationale: Circuit breaker opened repeatedly and retries were never checked, so client-side tuning is unverified.

remediation.action: Replace shallow /health checks with synthetic payment-path and TLS handshake checks for checkout-to-payment-service.
remediation.rationale: Current health checks reported healthy during the outage and cannot detect payment path failures or TLS problems.

remediation.action: Add alerting on payment provider error rate and circuit breaker state, with dashboards for checkout error rate by upstream call.
remediation.rationale: Onset was detected from aggregate error rates, and provider dependency signals would shorten detection.

remediation.action: Document and test a graceful degradation path for checkout when the payment provider is unavailable.
remediation.rationale: Checkout failures propagated fully to the gateway, indicating no isolation from a single provider outage.

brief.title: checkout and payment errors
brief.alert: ALERT [P1] checkout-service error rate 21% and api-gateway 5xx 8% since ~16:00 UTC. Customers report failed payments.

Telemetry covers 15:00 to 16:30 UTC; change history covers a longer window. Need to find the onset, the error signature, and whether a recent change or a downstream dependency (likely payment provider or payment-related service) is responsible.

A downstream payment provider or payment-service dependency degraded, causing checkout errors that propagate to api-gateway 5xx
An infrastructure event (capacity, network, certificate or timeout change) affecting checkout-to-payment connectivity
Upstream api-gateway routing or timeout change amplifying errors independently of checkout-service code

findings.summary: Checkout-service and api-gateway errors both step up abruptly in the 16:00 UTC bucket, from about 0.3% to about 21% (checkout) and about 7.7% (gateway). The checkout ERROR logs are dominated by 'payment-service returned 502 Bad Gateway' on order placement. The gateway's 502s are all on POST /api/v1/checkout, returned by upstream checkout-service. Gateway CPU, memory, latency and request rate stayed flat across the window. The sampled logs point to payment-service as the failing dependency, but I did not query payment-service directly.

observations.statement: checkout-service error_rate was flat at 0.24–0.35% from 15:00 to 15:55 UTC, then jumped to 21.17% at 16:00:00. It stayed between 19.85% and 22.47% through 16:30 (max 22.47% at 16:10, last 20.65%).
api-gateway error_rate was 0.33–0.45% from 15:00 to 15:55 UTC, then jumped to 7.73% at 16:00:00. It stayed between 7.47% and 8.28% through 16:30 (max 8.28% at 16:20).
The api-gateway step and the checkout-service step fall in the same 16:00 bucket at 5-minute resolution, so their relative order cannot be resolved from metrics alone.

api-gateway cpu_pct (36.7–39.3%), memory_pct (50–53.6%), latency_p99_ms (174–187 ms) and request_rate (406–432 req/s) show no step change at 16:00. Their 16:00 values are within their 15:00–15:55 ranges.

checkout-service ERROR logs in the 16:00–16:25 range are almost entirely 'order <id> failed: payment-service returned 502 Bad Gateway'. The first returned instance is at 16:00:27Z, and the errors recur at a steady cadence through 16:25:28Z.

Of the 62 checkout-service WARN/ERROR lines in the window, 60 are ERROR, all with the 'payment-service returned 502' signature (the 50 returned lines were all of this type). The only other checkout WARN is a single 'slow inventory reservation: 966ms' at 15:52:44Z, before the step.

api-gateway ERROR logs are 'upstream checkout-service returned 502 for POST /api/v1/checkout', first at 16:00:12Z and continuing to 16:30:00Z. The 30 returned lines all carry this signature and no other route. The only other gateway items are rate-limiter near-burst warnings and two slow /api/v1/search responses, which don't match the timing of the spike.

The gateway's first 502 log (16:00:12Z) precedes the earliest checkout ERROR returned (16:00:27Z). That ordering is only within the returned subset, because the checkout query was capped at 50 of 62 lines.

Errors concentrate on the payment step (POST /api/v1/checkout that calls payment-service) rather than on search or inventory. No checkout-side error signature referencing inventory or other upstream calls appeared in the sampled lines.

interpretations.statement: The checkout-service failures are caused by its call to payment-service returning 502, and api-gateway 5xx are a pass-through of checkout-service 502s, not an independent gateway fault. Gateway resource metrics are normal.

Onset is about 16:00:00 UTC for both services (within the 16:00 bucket), with no evidence of a gradual ramp beforehand. The gateway and checkout onsets appear simultaneous within the resolution of the data.
The gateway error_rate (~8%) is lower than checkout (~21%) because the gateway's denominator covers all routes, while only the checkout route is failing.
